races.name: Book Online At ripon-races.co.uk Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Napoleons Casino And Restaurant Leeds Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Kilfrush Blue
runners_data.note: Ruth Carr's runner has finished 8th and 9th on Good in its two starts and carries a 'fades in finish' flag — its natural style is true hold-up but it has been mapped to midfield as the field contains too many backmarkers to absorb; the STYLE_FIT flag tempers confidence in it delivering from whatever position it secures.

runners_data.name: Likeadyinwasp
runners_data.note: Three runs all at Southwell on AW stand-side bias trips give limited read across to turf soft ground at Ripon; Declan Carroll's 3-year-old is 49 days since its last run and has no evidence in the form book of handling today's surface, making its hold-up style particularly reliant on conditions playing into its hands.

runners_data.name: Grasmere Boy
runners_data.note: Julie Camacho's consistent sort has placed twice from two starts on Good and Good-to-Soft, showing a reliable front-running profile; the STYLE_FIT tag notes it is technically mapped slightly out of its purest role here, but with no credible challengers for the lead, it is almost certain to secure its natural front position and dictate terms.

runners_data.name: Masai Angel
runners_data.note: Richard & Fahey's runner has a soft-ground outing in its history (5th/6f/SOF) and has sim-going record of 1 win from 2 relevant starts, making it the most credible closer in the field on a stamina test; Billy Garritty takes the ride after 58 days off, and if the pace does stack up late, this hold-up type is best placed of the backmarkers.

runners_data.name: Kilfrush Desert
runners_data.note: Tom Eaves partners this Kevin Ryan-trained 3-year-old who has run just twice, placing 2nd and 3rd on AW and Good, and is stylistically unclassified (U); lightly raced and potentially ahead of what the bare form suggests, but the 58-day absence and unknown soft-ground handling are genuine questions on debut for the style and surface combination.

races.paceDynamic: Grasmere Boy is the confirmed front-runner here and, with only five runners and no credible challenger for the early lead, he can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the gates — particularly relevant on Good to Soft ground at Ripon where soft-ground stamina becomes a premium over 6f. The hold-up contingent of Kilfrush Blue, Likeadyinwasp, and Masai Angel will be tracking from behind, but the field holds more hold-up types than the race shape can comfortably accommodate at the rear, meaning Kilfrush Blue — mapped to midfield due to redistribution — is unlikely to secure its natural backmarker position. Kilfrush Desert is lightly raced and stylistically unclassified, adding a minor wild card to the positional picture. With one genuine pace-setter setting an uncontested, measured tempo on soft ground over a straight 6f, this race shape strongly favours prominent-to-mid racers who can track close to the pace and quicken in the final two furlongs, rather than pure closers who need a strong gallop to reel in the leader.

watchPoints.text: Grasmere Boy's jumping speed — if he misses the break, the entire race shape collapses and there is no replacement pace-setter in a five-runner field.
Kilfrush Blue's ability to find a workable position — mapped to midfield due to redistribution, if it drops to last on soft ground it faces a near-impossible task given its 'fades in finish' profile.

Ground conditions at Ripon — the going report consistently reads Good to Soft across all races, but soft-ground patches on the Ripon 6f straight can vary significantly and could catch out horses without proven soft form.

Kilfrush Desert's market move — as an unclassified lightly raced type with only two starts, any significant support in the market for Kevin Ryan's runner should be treated as live and meaningful information.

Masai Angel's soft-ground profile makes it the one hold-up runner with demonstrable evidence of handling conditions today, and it is worth monitoring its early position under Billy Garritty for signs of travelling smoothly.

races.name: Lloyd Land Rover Ripon Handicap (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Raulin
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse for David O'Meara who drops from shorter trips but has his best soft-ground form over 12-13f; faces a genuine task from the rear in a race where the front two are unlikely to come back to him in time, and his recent proximity figures of 6th and 7th don't inspire confidence.

runners_data.name: Winter Flower
runners_data.note: William Haggas runner returning after 53 days, which for this yard warrants respect; won over 10f and placed over 12f on soft/similar ground, but as a hold-up type she needs Something to crack — her most recent run was a disappointing 8th and she needs to bounce back sharply.

runners_data.name: Spirit Of Jura
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's runner has struggled in soft conditions (11th last time in similar going) and has run six times over today's trip without winning; a genuine deep hold-up type whose natural style leaves him with most to do in a race dominated by a lone, uncontested front-runner — the redistribution to midfield on the map reflects that he cannot get a natural position here.

runners_data.name: Something
runners_data.note: Liam Bailey's five-year-old is the race-shaper: straightforward front-runner who has won and placed over 12f on good ground, and the soft conditions have not stopped him showing form at the trip; recent headgear noted, quick turnaround from nine days ago is worth monitoring for freshness.

runners_data.name: Dream Harder
runners_data.note: Ian Williams' six-year-old has run six times in recent form without troubling the judge, returns from a lengthy 200-day absence, and though he handles soft in theory, his hold-up style is deeply disadvantaged in a race where a single front-runner controls the tempo — the long break and consistent losing runs make him difficult to trust even if he does get a position.

runners_data.name: Scottish Dancer
runners_data.note: Tim Reed's seven-year-old steps down considerably in trip from his last run (20f) but has won over 14f on good ground and finished second over 16f — the drop in distance suits his prominent style better than a staying test, and with the claim of Millie Wonnacott (5lb) he carries the lightest weight in the race on an attractive mark.

races.paceDynamic: Something is the sole confirmed front-runner in a six-runner field and will set sail from the gates, establishing a lead over 1m4f on good to soft ground at Ripon with no meaningful pace rival to push him along. Scottish Dancer is the only other prominent-profile runner and will likely tuck in behind Something, meaning the front two effectively control the tempo and dictate terms from the outset. The hold-up contingent — Raulin, Winter Flower, Spirit Of Jura, and Dream Harder — will be anchored in the rear half, needing Something to either burn out or for the ground to extract enough stamina-sapping effort to bring them back into it late. This field contains more hold-up types than the race shape can naturally accommodate; Spirit Of Jura and Dream Harder are true hold-up horses repositioned to midfield on the map, but Something and Scottish Dancer are the pair most likely to actually hold their natural prominent positions. The race shape strongly favours a prominent-to-lead profile: with one controlling pace setter, a manageable tempo, and soft ground that rewards relaxed racers over those scrambling from the rear, horses who can track Something closely will be first to capitalise if he weakens, making the prominent-to-mid profile the primary beneficiary.

scenarios.title: Something Controls, Prominent Benefits
scenarios.trigger: If Something secures the lead unchallenged and sets a measured but not suicidal gallop on the soft ground.
scenarios.body: If Something secures the lead unchallenged and sets a measured but not suicidal gallop on the soft ground.

scenarios.title: Hold-Up Closers Reel Them In

scenarios.body: If Something's front-running effort proves unsustainable on the soft ground and the pace proves genuinely hot enough to string the field out.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Something Outstays All
scenarios.trigger: If the tempo is truly moderate and Something finds his stamina reserves untapped, stealing a decisive lead into the straight.
scenarios.body: If the tempo is truly moderate and Something finds his stamina reserves untapped, stealing a decisive lead into the straight.

scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Chaos Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves so slow that the race turns into a sprint finish from the final two furlongs, negating positional advantages entirely.
scenarios.body: If the pace proves so slow that the race turns into a sprint finish from the final two furlongs, negating positional advantages entirely.

watchPoints.text: Scottish Dancer has the lightest weight in the race with the 5lb claim and a win over today's trip — watch whether Wonnacott gets him into the slipstream of Something early, as this is the horse best placed to capitalise if the front-runner weakens.

Dream Harder returns from 200 days off for Ian Williams — monitor market moves as a fitness concern; if he drifts in the ring his chance is effectively redundant given his hold-up style and losing run in recent form.

Something ran just nine days ago — watch his coat and demeanour in the paddock for signs of a quick turnaround catching up with him, as any drop in his front-running zeal hands the race to a less obvious winner.

Winter Flower is the Haggas runner returning from 53 days; this stable can be sharp with well-bred horses off a break, and her one soft-ground placing over 12f is the key piece of form to monitor if the race develops slowly enough for her to get involved.

With only six runners on soft ground over 1m4f, watch the pace between the 3f and 1f markers — if Something still has a clear lead at the furlong pole, prominent rivals cannot be expected to close him down in time.

races.name: Wells Memorial Challenge Trophy Handicap

runners_data.name: Blind Beggar
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old hold-up performer with just 6/15 and no wins on similar going; Ryan Kavanagh's 5lb claim is a useful weight advantage, but 25 days since last run and a poor recent string (05-000) suggests he arrives out of form and is likely to need a stronger pace than this race will generate.

runners_data.name: Beyond Borders
runners_data.note: Won last time out over six furlongs on standard ground and Hart is a polished jockey, but a hold-up horse who has placed only twice in fifteen starts on similar going (0W0P soft) and faces a race shape that may not generate enough pace for him to pounce late.

runners_data.name: Glory Hyde
runners_data.note: Arrives on the back of a strong recent sequence including three wins in her last six starts; Joanna Mason's good course knowledge and Roger Fell's yard in fair nick (1/11 over 14 days) make this a serious front-running proposition, though her soft-ground record of 1W1P from three similar-going starts is modest and worth monitoring.

runners_data.name: Beattie Is Back
runners_data.note: Fahey yard is active (4/50 over 14 days) and this seven-year-old has placed at this trip before; has no wins on soft from recent history and is ideally suited racing prominently where he can press the pace rather than chasing it, making Glory Hyde's clear lead the main threat to his chance.

runners_data.name: Mark's Choice
runners_data.note: A prolific recent winner at five and six furlongs (two wins in last five) and wears cheekpieces for the first time in a while; his natural hold-up style is shifted toward midfield here because the mapping cannot place all hold-up types at the rear, meaning he may not get his usual patient tactical run in a small field at a steady pace.

runners_data.name: Bye Law
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's three-year-old is the youngest in the field and has shown consistent form at six furlongs on soft (four runs in similar conditions); races prominently by nature but is shown in midfield on this map because more prominent types are present than the pace shape can accommodate, which may mean he runs closer to the pace than his mapped position implies.

races.paceDynamic: Glory Hyde is the sole confirmed front-runner in this six-horse field and, with only Beattie Is Back as a genuine prominent challenger, faces minimal pressure for the lead on soft ground over six furlongs at Ripon. With no rival likely to seriously contest pace-setting duties from flag to first bend, Glory Hyde can control tempo at a rate that suits her own stamina profile rather than being wound up by a rival. The soft going and flat Ripon track will allow early fractions to be managed, meaning the race is set up for a rail-hugging, prominent-to-lead shape where those tracking the pace closely will have the clearest path to victory. This shape strongly favours prominent racers and early-to-mid movers who can capitalise on a regulated tempo — pure hold-up horses and late finishers will find the sectionals insufficiently strong to create the gap they need. Note that Bye Law and Mark's Choice are genuine prominent and hold-up types respectively who have been mapped to midfield because the field contains more such runners than the map can accommodate at the rear; Glory Hyde and Beattie Is Back are most likely to actually secure the positions closest to the pace.

scenarios.body: If Glory Hyde breaks cleanly and dictates a manageable tempo on soft ground, her rivals are unable to pressurise her.

watchPoints.text: Glory Hyde — watch for a clean break from the stalls; if she misses the kick, Beattie Is Back could steal an uncontested lead and the entire shape of the race changes.

Bye Law — his true prominent style means he may push forward from the mapped midfield position in the early stages, potentially creating an unplanned contest for pace that unsettles Glory Hyde's control.
Mark's Choice — cheekpieces on a 10-year-old in soft ground merit watching in the paddock; if he shows freshness and breaks alertly he could take a different position to his mapped midfield slot.

Beyond Borders — the small field of six means hold-up horses will have limited runners to weave through in the final furlong; watch whether Jason Hart elects to race closer to the pace than normal to compensate.

Going — the going report states Good To Soft for all 6f races on the card, but each successive race on the same ground and rail line can soften conditions; if earlier races suggest any deterioration, soft-ground stamina moves up in importance for this contest.

races.name: Sky Sports Racing Sky 415 Fillies' Handicap

runners_data.name: Krissy
runners_data.note: Sole front-runner here and likely to get an uncontested lead, which suits a mare who has won three of her last five — her soft-ground form reads only one win from 15 on similar going, which is the chief concern, but her ability to dictate from the front at this trip is a significant compensating factor; OR 70 is a career high.

runners_data.name: Bay Dream Believer
runners_data.note: Won over 10f on good ground last time and holds the second-most prominent position in this field with Jason Hart aboard; she carries headgear (hood) and will need to improve past a soft-ground placing record that shows just one placed run from four tries, but her prominent style gives her every chance in this tactical setup.

runners_data.name: Rosemary May
runners_data.note: Has been placed in soft conditions before and Tim Easterby's runners have been busy, with eight winners from 91 over 14 days — she is flagged as fading in the finish and runs only nine days after her last outing; in truth a natural hold-up runner who will be forced to sit closer to the pace than she prefers, diluting her finishing effectiveness, and her recent form shows a string of single-figure finishes.

runners_data.name: The New Bay Pearl
runners_data.note: Runs without a confirmed soft-ground win and her entire recent history is on standard artificial tracks, making the going here an unknown quantity for Simon Whitaker's filly; naturally inclined to race from the rear, she will find herself mapped into midfield ahead of her comfort zone, which compounds the uncertainty around her turf and going adaptability.

runners_data.name: Melody De Vega
runners_data.note: Drops from OR 70-rated company and has a solid placed record over this sort of trip — three seconds and a third in her last five suggest she is knocking on the door; races from a hold-up position but Dr Newland and Insole's filly has shown she can travel well in midfield and could prove the most dangerous finisher if the pace is testing enough.

runners_data.name: Eloquencia
runners_data.note: Three runs, three places — an unexposed filly with a pee-pattern of consistent front-placing that suggests she can sit handy and challenge late; Joanna Mason takes the ride and the horse is rated OR 68 with an unresolved style tag, but recent form over 10f and 11f on good and standard ground is encouraging for this trip; the question is whether soft ground blunts her finishing kick.

runners_data.name: Angela's Baar
runners_data.note: Ran in soft ground nine days ago and finished eighth — the back-to-back soft-ground assignments are a concern for a filly whose best form has been on good and standard surfaces; Adrian Keatley's three-year-old holds an OR of 67 and races from a hold-up position, which is not ideal given the pace shape, and the quick return after a below-par effort adds to the risk.

runners_data.name: Glasgow Kiss
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer has been active and the booking of Billy Garritty is fair, but this filly's form over 8f on soft ground — one run, no win, no place — is not encouraging; a natural hold-up type pushed into a midfield map position she cannot naturally exploit, and her best results have come on good or standard over 7f, making the step up in trip on this going a double unknown.

races.paceDynamic: Krissy is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival to contest early supremacy, she is expected to slot onto the lead and dictate a controlled, measured gallop over this 1m2f on good-to-soft ground. Bay Dream Believer is the only other prominent-style runner and will likely track Krissy in second, meaning the early tempo is set by just two horses without any pressure to force a genuine test. This creates a slow-to-moderate pace dynamic that favours those racing handy — Krissy and Bay Dream Believer gain positional advantage cheaply, while the hold-up contingent is forced to make up ground from further back when the pace inevitably picks up in the straight. The field carries a significant volume of true hold-up types — Rosemary May, The New Bay Pearl, and Glasgow Kiss are all natural closers who are mapped to midfield here simply because the rear of the field is overcrowded, and they are unlikely to get the clean, late-running position their style demands. The tactical verdict is clear: a compact, front-to-prominent running profile suits this race shape, with Krissy and Bay Dream Believer best positioned to exploit a lack of pressure throughout.

watchPoints.text: Krissy leads unchallenged — if Rhys Elliott (5lb claim) allows her to bowl along at her own pace without interference from Bay Dream Believer, the advantage she gains for free could prove decisive on a track where the leader is notoriously hard to peg back over 1m2f.

Melody De Vega is the most likely hold-up danger — of the genuine closers in the field she has the most consistent placed form at this sort of trip and could be the one to mount a credible late challenge if the gallop is strong enough to bring her into it.

Eloquencia's undefined style is a tactical wildcard — if Joanna Mason elects to track up into a prominent position rather than drop in, she could be racing closer to the pace than expected and her unbeaten placed record suggests she handles racing on the front end.

The volume of soft-ground debutants in this field is notable — The New Bay Pearl, Glasgow Kiss, and Angela's Baar all have limited or no evidence of performing on today's going, meaning a rain-softened surface may thin the field's competitive depth and concentrate the outcome among those who have already shown they handle cut.

Bay Dream Believer's headgear (hood) is worth monitoring at the stalls and in the early stages — if it sharpens her early, she may push Krissy harder than expected and inadvertently create a slightly stronger gallop that brings the midfield types into play.

races.name: We're Back For Ladies' Day Tomorrow Handicap

runners_data.name: Brain Freeze
runners_data.note: Three-year-old with a soft-ground win on his form string, ridden by claimer Rhys Elliott; a genuine hold-up type but with only two runs in similar going from eight attempts, the evidence base is thin and his 6f-heavy history is a mild trip concern at 5f.

runners_data.name: Arlington
runners_data.note: Five-year-old whose five most recent runs are all on Tapeta at 5f, so turf soft-ground form is effectively absent; his true instinct is to come from off the pace but with the field so packed, he cannot fulfil that role and the style-fit discount applies.

runners_data.name: Dunnington Lad
runners_data.note: Six-year-old returning just nine days after his last run for a trainer with a modest recent record; his form over soft ground is poor (0 wins, 0 places from two qualifying runs) and he sits out of position relative to his natural trailing style.

runners_data.name: Barmyblade
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby handler whose 10/113 T14 strike rate signals live stable form; placed on soft going once from three attempts at the trip, wears headgear and is one of the less extreme hold-up types — he may drift closer than expected and that positional advantage matters here.

runners_data.name: You Mystify Me
runners_data.note: Three-year-old for the Easterby yard ridden by Joanna Mason, wearing a visor; a second and a third in her short form string show she runs her races and her good-ground 5f placed effort is the key asset, though soft conditions are untested and the unknown factor is real.

runners_data.name: Doralee
runners_data.note: Five-year-old whose entire soft-ground sample (one run from 15 in similar conditions) produced a single placed effort; she is a natural hold-up mare whose redistribution to midfield reflects that every rear position is oversubscribed, making her style fit structurally compromised in this shape.

runners_data.name: Hyrcanian
runners_data.note: Carries a specific finishing concern — flagged as fading in the finish — which is a serious liability in a race where every horse is being pushed forward and the dash home is the entire contest; his soft-ground profile (0 wins, 0 places from three) compounds the concern.

runners_data.name: What A Tahoo
runners_data.note: Three-year-old from the powerful Fahey yard with a consistent form string of 947433 showing he hits the frame regularly; six-furlong form is the bulk of his CV so the drop to 5f on soft ground introduces a stamina-in-reverse query, but trainer's 7/60 T14 rate keeps him relevant.

runners_data.name: Tanaka
runners_data.note: David O'Meara three-year-old whose single soft-ground qualifying run produced a poor return; wears headgear, is one of the lightest-weighted runners at 124lbs, and the trainer's 9/49 recent strike rate is respectable, but form of 5640-7 does not inspire confidence he can dominate this.

races.paceDynamic: With every single runner in this nine-horse field carrying a hold-up profile, there is no confirmed front-runner and no horse expected to stride into a natural lead — the race will drift off the tape before reluctant pace-setters are dragged to the front. On soft ground over a flat Ripon 5f, the lack of any genuine pace influence means the early gallop will be honest at best and crawling at worst, compressing the field and creating a sprint-finish dynamic from halfway. Barmyblade, You Mystify Me and Brain Freeze hold the least extreme hold-up profiles and are most likely to find themselves closer to the action than they would choose. In a field where every runner is a true hold-up type redistibuted across the map — with Arlington, Doralee, What A Tahoo, Tanaka and Hyrcanian among those unable to fulfil their natural rear position — whoever secures the best tactical ground in the bunch and produces the sharpest late surge will dictate the outcome; the profile that benefits is the runner who can race prominently by default and sustain a sprint on soft ground, rather than any genuine closer needing a true pace to run into.

watchPoints.text: Barmyblade and You Mystify Me are the two runners most likely to accidentally secure an uncontested lead — if either edges forward in the early stages, the entire race shape tilts in their favour.

Hyrcanian is flagged as a horse that fades in finishes and carries a style-fit discount; if the race is a pure sprint from 2f out he is the runner most at risk of being swamped and punters should not be surprised by a poor effort.

Arlington's five most recent runs are all on artificial surfaces — watch whether he handles the soft Ripon turf, as a horse coming off an all-weather campaign into these conditions is an unknown quantity even if the style-fit issue is set aside.

The going report consistently reads Good To Soft across all Ripon races this evening, so despite the declared SOFT description the track may be riding faster than the official going — any runner with a specific soft-ground angle should be assessed with that caveat in mind.

With seven of nine runners carrying a style-fit or redistribution flag, draw and early positioning off the stalls at Ripon's 5f start could outweigh running style entirely — watch the early stall break as a key race-shaping moment.
